suggestions: Collapse the five independent lookbacks (30, 90, 7, 90, 90) into one economic horizon—e.g., 20 or 63 days—for range normalization Ma(high-low), volume baseline Ma(volume), trend filter Ma(close-open), and final Ts_Zscore. The current mosaic of windows is the main remaining degrees-of-freedom surface: each length can be tuned to in-sample co-movement without adding distinct information (efficiency, liquidity, drift are all medium-term phenomena). A single timescale reduces combinatorial fitting risk and should improve validation rank_ic, which is already negative (-0.0063) despite a small positive train IC.

Remove the intermediate Rank(...,90) wrapped around Ma(...,7) and keep exactly one cross-sectional compression step at the outermost layer: Zscore(Rank(raw_signal, N), N) with raw_signal = ((close-open)/Ma(high-low,N)) * (volume/Ma(volume,N)) * trend_weight, optionally summed over 5 days via Decaylinear instead of Ma(7). Sequential Ma → Rank → Zscore → Rank applies three nonlinear rescalings each with its own window—a classic overfitting pattern from the search tree that survived the monotonicity pass. One rank at the end preserves outlier control while cutting redundant transforms that fit bucket boundaries to training noise.

Replace the hard gate Sign(Ma(close-open,30)) with a continuous trend-alignment weight, e.g., Ma(close-open,N) / (Ma(Abs(close-open),N) + epsilon) or Tanh(Ma(close-open,N)/Ts_Std(close-open,N)). Sign creates a discontinuous on/off switch: a one-day change in the 30-day mean flips the entire signal and makes quintile membership hypersensitive to the trend window on holdout data. A bounded continuous weight still rewards volume-backed range efficiency only when open-to-close drift is persistent, but avoids brittle threshold effects and removes an implicit binary hyperparameter from the formula.
